text.tspan: The top panel illustrates an existing two-stage method
for classifying real versus generated images.
In the first stage, input image x is processed by a diffusion
model to generate a reconstructed image, x prime.
Separated by a structural barrier, both the original image
and its reconstruction pass forward to stage two.
An absolute operation creates a residual map, fed into
a classifier to predict whether the image is real or generated.
Crucially, this existing pipeline operates without
interaction between the first and second stages.
The bottom panel presents our proposed method,
organized around end-to-end training.
Here, the input image x passes through an FMRE module
to produce a secondary pseudo image x_pse.
Both image streams are sent through the shared diffusion model,
generating reconstructed outputs for each branch.
Dual absolute operations compute residual maps for
both the original stream and the pseudo stream.
The two residual maps are concatenated and delivered
to the classifier for final real/generated prediction.
Joint end-to-end training aligns the diffusion model and
classifier, leading to better overall alignment.
